items.followUp: State two functions of enzymes in living organisms.

rubric.why: An enzyme’s main function is to catalyze, or speed up, chemical reactions.
rubric.description: Enzymes catalyze chemical reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes speed up or catalyze reactions.

rubric.why: Enzymes are also used in processes such as digestion and in various industries.
rubric.description: A valid second use of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one valid use or application, such as digestion, food processing, detergents, or medicine.

modelAnswer: Enzymes catalyze chemical reactions in living organisms, such as the breakdown of food during digestion.
They are also used in applications such as food processing, detergents, and medicine.
A different valid use may be given.

items.followUp: State two roles of enzymes in digestion.

rubric.why: The definition should identify photosynthesis as the process by which plants make food using light energy.
rubric.description: Defines photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition including food or glucose production by plants using light.

rubric.why: The equation should show carbon dioxide and water forming glucose and oxygen.
rubric.description: Gives the balanced photosynthesis equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct equation or its correctly named reactants and products; light and chlorophyll may be shown above the arrow.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
6CO₂ + 6H₂O  —light and chlorophyll→  C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

items.followUp: What is alcoholic fermentation, and under what conditions does it occur?

rubric.why: Lactic acid fermentation is an anaerobic breakdown of glucose.
rubric.description: Identifies the process as anaerobic glucose breakdown.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that glucose is broken down without oxygen.

rubric.why: The process forms lactic acid and may occur in muscle cells or certain bacteria.
rubric.description: Names the product or a valid site of lactic acid fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming lactic acid as the product or giving a valid example such as muscles or bacteria.

modelAnswer: Lactic acid fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose in which lactic acid is produced.
It can occur in muscle cells when oxygen is insufficient and in some bacteria.

items.followUp: Describe the cellular and organ levels of organization in an organism.

rubric.why: The molecular level is built from atoms and molecules, including biological molecules.
rubric.description: Explains the molecular level of organization.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks: 1 for atoms forming molecules and 1 for identifying molecules or biomolecules as the basis of this level.

rubric.why: A tissue consists of similar cells organized together.
rubric.description: Defines a tissue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a tissue as a group of similar cells.

rubric.why: The cells in a tissue work together to perform a function.
rubric.description: States the function of a tissue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the cells work together to perform a specific function.

rubric.why: A suitable example demonstrates the tissue level of organization.
rubric.description: Gives an example of a tissue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any valid animal or plant tissue example.

modelAnswer: At the molecular level, atoms combine to form molecules, including the biomolecules found in organisms.
These molecules form the chemical basis of cells and their components.
At the tissue level, a group of similar cells is organized together.
The cells work together to perform a specific function.
Examples of tissues include muscle, nervous, epithelial, and connective tissues in animals, and xylem and phloem in plants.

items.followUp: Explain how an enzyme acts on its substrate and what happens to the enzyme afterward.

rubric.why: An enzyme has an active site whose shape is specific to its substrate.
rubric.description: Identifies the enzyme’s active site and substrate specificity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a specific active site or its fit with a particular substrate.

rubric.why: The substrate binds at the active site, forming an enzyme-substrate complex.
rubric.description: Describes formation of the enzyme-substrate complex.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the substrate binds to the enzyme or that an enzyme-substrate complex forms.

rubric.why: The enzyme facilitates the reaction, commonly by lowering the activation energy.
rubric.description: Explains how the enzyme facilitates the reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the enzyme lowers activation energy or speeds up the reaction.

rubric.why: The substrate is changed into product or products.
rubric.description: States that products are formed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying conversion of the substrate into products.

rubric.why: The enzyme is not used up in the reaction and can act again.
rubric.description: States that the enzyme remains unchanged and reusable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the enzyme is released unchanged or can be reused.

modelAnswer: An enzyme has an active site with a shape specific to its substrate.
The substrate binds to the active site, forming an enzyme-substrate complex.
The enzyme facilitates the reaction by lowering its activation energy.
The substrate is converted into product or products, which are released from the active site.
The enzyme remains unchanged and can be reused.

items.followUp: Explain how light energy is captured and used during photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Chlorophyll is the pigment that absorbs light energy.
rubric.description: States the role of chlorophyll in absorbing light.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying chlorophyll as the light-absorbing pigment.

rubric.why: Light supplies the energy required for photosynthesis.
rubric.description: States the role of light as an energy source.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that light provides energy for photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Absorbed light energy is converted into chemical energy.
rubric.description: Describes conversion of light energy to chemical energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that light energy is converted into chemical energy.

rubric.why: Light energy supports water splitting and the reactions that produce glucose from carbon dioxide.
rubric.description: Gives a further role of light energy in photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning water splitting (photolysis) or the use of the captured energy in glucose formation.

modelAnswer: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that absorbs light energy.
Light provides the energy needed for photosynthesis.
The absorbed light energy is converted into chemical energy.
This energy supports the splitting of water and the formation of glucose from carbon dioxide.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a monomer and a polymer.

rubric.why: Micromolecules are relatively small and have low molecular mass.
rubric.description: Describes micromolecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying micromolecules as small, simple, or low-molecular-mass molecules.

rubric.why: A valid example supports the distinction between micromolecules and macromolecules.
rubric.description: Gives an example of a micromolecule or macromolecule, or describes macromolecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example of either class or for stating that macromolecules are large, complex, high-molecular-mass molecules.

modelAnswer: Micromolecules are small, simple molecules with relatively low molecular mass, such as water or glucose.
Macromolecules are large, complex molecules with high molecular mass, such as proteins, nucleic acids, and many carbohydrates.

items.followUp: Name one contribution of Jabir-bin-Hayan and give the names of two books written by him.

rubric.why: Jabir-bin-Hayan is identified as a Muslim scientist and is commonly known as the father of chemistry.
rubric.description: Identifies Jabir-bin-Hayan.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying him as a scientist or as the father of chemistry.

rubric.why: The two books named in the textbook are Al-Kimya and Kitab al-Sab'een.
rubric.description: Names two books by Jabir-bin-Hayan.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving both book titles; accept reasonable spelling variants.

modelAnswer: Jabir-bin-Hayan was a Muslim scientist known as the father of chemistry.
Two books associated with him are Al-Kimya and Kitab al-Sab'een.
